text:
joan: noticed weird 429s on /v1/generate for a handful of tenants; gRPC backend counts look low. gateway is doing transcode. anyone seen mapping/quotas mismatch?
ravi: if gateway transcode drops the canonical rpc descriptor, quota service might key on http path but backend thinks differently. what's our current gateway rule?
joan: current rule: - match: POST /v1/generate to: GenerationService.Generate (no extra headers)
tasha: two immediate fixes: 1) gateway injects an internal-only header like X-Canonical-RPC=GenerationService.Generate (fast), 2) enforce quotas after transcode inside gRPC stack (more correct but larger rollout).
kevin: header approach ok but must be non-spoofable. gateway should sign header or set it on an internal-only channel so client cannot spoof. Also add a fallback to http path for a month.
selena: Console/telemetry request: add both labels 'ingress_path' and 'canonical_rpc' in metrics so we can show a delta panel. Also add a per-route toggle to choose "billing source" (path vs rpc).
joan: rollout plan suggestion: 1) canary gateway header injection at 5% for affected routes, 2) metrics exporter add 'canonical_rpc' and 'protocol=transcoded|grpc', 3) console expose toggle and comparison chart, 4) after 3w telemetry parity flip enforcement.
quota-bot: quota-service: canary tagging enabled for /v1/generate (5%). Logs forwarded to telemetry-raw for comparison.
ravi: add integrity via HMAC header X-Method-Signature validated by quota service; file INFRA-1437 for key provisioning.
kevin: add alert: if canonical_rpc vs ingress_path counts differ by >15% for a route during canary, capture sampled traces and page on-call.
selena: will add UI note: switching quota key can cause transient alerts/billing diffs; recommend gradual rollout and monitor per-tenant deltas.
joan: cool. I'll open RFC and tickets for gateway change, exporter label work, console toggle, and alerting. tag me on infra/key ticket.
kevin: one more: watch cardinality. canonical_rpc is ok short-term but add protocol label so long-term retention can cap cardinality.
joan: agreed. thanks everyone. If no objections I'll start the canary tomorrow morning. :rocket:
